episode: From Drab to Fab, Revamping a Dark Kitchen into a Gorgeous Cooking Space
assessment: A basement kitchen and family room in a pool house. The before detail is the one worth leading on: the kitchen sat on an outside wall and ran so cold that the owners left two cupboard doors open through the winter to keep the pipes from freezing. The finished kitchen has a raised ceiling, a window cut in over the sink that was never there, alder cabinets by the family's own cabinet maker, and a backsplash Mike says runs about twice the cost of a normal one and only looks beveled. The usable finished footage is 11:22 to 13:55.

project_context.summary: A dated basement kitchen and family room in a pool house. The lighted ceiling came out and the ceiling went up about a foot, a window was cut in over the sink, and the room was filled with recessed cans. Alder cabinets by the family's own cabinet maker, granite counters, a brick pattern backsplash that runs all the way up and around, a black composite farmhouse sink, a faucet whose pull down tucks away out of sight, a microwave behind a lift up cabinet door, a built in spice rack beside the dishwasher, and a cooktop with a separate wall oven under it in the island. The family room behind it got a built in entertainment cabinet, surround sound, new lighting and a two step crown.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, cut from 11:22 to 13:55. Nothing from the sneak preview at 9:07, because the appliances and fixtures are not installed in it.
notes: The cold cupboard doors are the hook. Mike explains them at 1:14 over the before footage, and the Short says it over the finished room instead.
Separate oven and cooktop meant a second 220 line had to be run from the garage panel after the job was finished. Good material for a second Short, left out of this one for room.

shot_notes: Mike works the right of frame through most of the finished walkthrough, so the clean windows are mostly left hand crops. The ones found by scanning: the kitchen wide at 11:28 to 11:34, the window and sink at 11:36 to 11:50, the upper cabinets at 11:52 to 11:56, the microwave cabinet open at 11:57 to 12:00, the island with its cooktop and oven at 12:04 to 12:16 held right, the faucet close at 13:04 to 13:08 held left, the sink and rug wide at 12:50 to 12:58, and the family room at 13:20 to 13:30.

shorts.full_vo:
This basement kitchen was so cold they left two cupboard doors open all winter. Just to keep the pipes in the outside wall from freezing. We tore out the old lighted ceiling and picked up about a foot of height.

Then we put a window in over the sink that was never there before. The cabinets are alder, built by the family's own cabinet maker. That backsplash runs all the way up and around.

It looks beveled, but it isn't, and it costs about double a normal one. Black farmhouse sink, and the faucet hides its own pull down. The microwave sits behind a door that lifts up out of the way.

The island has a cooktop with a separate oven underneath. Tile floor, can lights right through, and the family room opens off the back. From a dark basement kitchen to this.
shorts.voice_direction: Warm and unhurried, a contractor showing a friend a room he is pleased with, and enjoying the cupboard door detail.

shorts.framing_note: view is the share of the source width each shot shows. Full bleed is 31.6 percent of a 16:9 frame blown up 1.78 times, and Mike flagged it twice as zoomed in with no perspective. Each shot carries the widest view that still reads and still keeps Mike a figure in the room rather than the subject; the tight crops were what kept him out, so wide rooms without him go to 0.80, bar and vanity runs with him at the edge sit at 0.45 to 0.60. Chosen off scripts/frame_views.py, not a flat number.
shorts.full_bleed_note: A second cut built with --full-bleed --variant fullbleed. Every shot fills the canvas, and the perspective comes from the move: fb_pan sweeps each window across the clean part of its take, wide rooms travelling half the frame, Mike's side of a take left alone. The two cuts share the script, the VO and the takes, and differ only in framing.
